tasks.short: Look up the site and earlier visits, inspect the site for space, power and cable routes, discuss location and construction needs with the customer, and write the site survey.

steps.what: Telecom technician looks up the site address, maps and earlier visits before going
Telecom technician determines viability of sites through observation of space, power and cable routes
Telecom technician discusses site locations and construction requirements with customers
Telecom technician writes the site survey with sketches and photos: as notes typed into a report afterwards today, once on the tablet checklist after the change

tasks.design: The work order in the field service app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) shows the site on a map with photos and notes from earlier visits. The site survey is a checklist on the tablet with photo fields, so no report is typed afterwards. Inspecting the site and talking with the customer stay with the technician; location data are used for the job, not to track the technician.
tasks.previous_blocker: Earlier visits were looked up in several places and surveys written up by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Field service apps hold site history, checklists and photos per job.
tasks.still_hard: Every building is different; the checklist only covers the routine part.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the cable route the building plans do not show.

reach.learn: Whether checklist surveys cut return visits.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy offers work orders that fill themselves in and checklists for technicians.
Workflow systems and GPS in vans are staff tracking systems that need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work order to the site survey; installation is outside.
Input contract: work orders from the project planner; site history from earlier jobs; fallback is paper notes.

Inspecting and discussing keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for reading the site history on the map; s4 keeps 65 because the typed write-up goes and the findings, sketches and photos are still made by the technician.

incremental.description: Telecom technician tags photos to checklist items.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a new site with no earlier jobs in the app, so background is gathered as today (6.2); high: a site with history (12.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Search manufacturer manuals and specifications, review permits and local rules, determine equipment requirements and procedures, and note them on the work order.

steps.what: Telecom technician searches manufacturer manuals and technical specifications for the equipment

loop.input: The technician's question and the manuals and specifications for the equipment model on the work order.
loop.output: An answer quoting the passage and page it rests on, or no answer.
loop.check: Code shows only answers with a quoted passage and page from that model's manual. The technician reads the passage to confirm it says what the answer states; unclear or unsupported answers are looked up in the manual.
loop.stop: One answer per question; without a quoted passage the technician searches the manual.
loop.why_not_simpler: Technicians ask in their own words; manuals run to hundreds of pages.

steps.what: Telecom technician reviews building permits and ordinances for the site
Telecom technician determines communication equipment requirements and procedures for the job
Telecom technician notes requirements and parts on the work order

tasks.design: An answer desk over the manufacturer manuals and specifications for the equipment on the work order answers the technician's questions with the quoted passage and page. Permits and local rules are read by the technician. Requirements and parts go on the work order in the field service app ({OPS_SYSTEM}) as fixed fields with part numbers from the catalogue.
tasks.previous_blocker: Long manuals were searched by hand for each model.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models answer from given manuals with quoted passages.
tasks.still_hard: Older equipment has scanned manuals that search badly.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing the manual's procedure does not fit this building.
tasks.altitude: The technician reads quoted passages instead of whole manuals.

reach.learn: Whether the answer desk cuts calls to seniors.

evidence.claim: Language models can answer from a given manual and quote the passage and page.
Manufacturers publish installation manuals and specifications per equipment model.

assumptions: Boundary: from the work order to the updated work order; installation is outside.
Input contract: manuals from manufacturers kept by the technical support team; work orders from the planner; fallback is searching PDFs.

Permits and requirements stay with the technician and keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for reading quoted passages and checking unclear ones; s4 keeps 75 because part numbers come from the catalogue and the requirements are still written by the technician.
The answer desk sees no customer data.
research_questions: How often is the quoted passage the right one?

already_counted.description: Telecom technician reads the quoted passages.

incremental.description: Telecom technician reports wrong or outdated answers.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: manuals for older models are not loaded, so most searches stay in PDFs (8.0); high: manuals loaded for the equipment in use (20.2).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Receive the fault ticket, read alarms and run remote line tests, diagnose and correct the fault remotely, and write the cause and fix in the ticket.

steps.what: Telecom technician receives the fault ticket from the network operations centre
Telecom technician reads alarms and runs remote line tests to find the sources of problems
Telecom technician diagnoses and corrects problems remotely by resetting or reconfiguring equipment
Telecom technician writes the fault cause and fix in the ticket

loop.input: The technician's dictated note on the fault and the fix.
loop.output: Fields for fault, cause, action and parts.
loop.check: Code checks required fields are filled and part numbers exist in the catalogue. The technician reads each field against the dictated note and the fix done; any field the note does not support is left blank for the technician to fill.
loop.stop: Confirmed by the technician, or after one failed retry the technician types the fields.
loop.why_not_simpler: Dictated notes vary; fixed parsing misses fields.

tasks.design: Fault tickets arrive with the related alarms attached. The network management system ({OPS_SYSTEM}) groups alarms by location and runs standard line tests on the affected port, showing results next to the ticket. The technician diagnoses and corrects the fault. The technician still states the cause and fix; a bounded step turns the dictated note into fault, cause, action and parts fields, which the technician reads against the note before closing.
tasks.previous_blocker: Alarms and tests were read on separate screens and notes typed into tickets.
tasks.enabler_now: Network management systems group alarms and run remote tests; models can extract fields from a dictated note.
tasks.still_hard: Intermittent faults do not show in a single test.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising a fault pattern from an outage years ago.

reach.learn: Whether coded causes show repeat faults.

evidence.claim: Network management systems group alarms by location and run remote line tests.
Workflow systems that can track staff need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the fault ticket to the closed ticket; site visits are outside.
Input contract: fault reports from the network operations centre; parts catalogue from the warehouse; fallback is typed notes.

Diagnosing and correcting keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for reading the ticket with its alarms; s2 keeps 70 for choosing and reading tests; s4 keeps 80 because the technician still states cause and fix and only field entry and part look-up go.
Ticket data are not used to rate technicians.
research_questions: Do repeat faults get spotted sooner?

already_counted.description: Telecom technician confirms the extracted fields.

incremental.description: Telecom technician reports misgrouped alarms to the network team.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: older equipment where alarms group poorly and standard tests do not run, so reading and testing stay largely by hand (12.0); high: equipment covered by the grouped alarms and tests (19.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Phone the base for the next job and instructions, call colleagues or vendors for technical advice, report equipment status by radio, and confirm job completion with the base.

steps.what: Telecom technician phones the base to receive the next job and instructions
Telecom technician calls senior technicians or the vendor for technical advice
Telecom technician reports equipment status to the base by two-way radio
Telecom technician confirms job completion with the base by phone

tasks.design: The next job and its instructions arrive in the field service app ({OPS_SYSTEM}), assigned by rules on skills, distance and availability, not on behaviour. The technician sets equipment status and job completion with buttons and short notes, which the base sees at once. Calls for technical advice and radio contact for urgent matters stay.
tasks.previous_blocker: Jobs, status and completion all went through phone and radio calls to the base.
tasks.enabler_now: Field service apps push jobs and take status updates from the technician.
tasks.still_hard: Basements and remote sites often have no mobile coverage.
tasks.human_edge: Explaining to a senior colleague what the equipment is doing when it fits no error code.

reach.learn: Whether app status updates cut calls to the base.

evidence.claim: FieldBuddy offers job assignment and scheduling for field technicians.
GPS and workflow systems in vans are staff tracking systems that need works council consent.
AI that allocates jobs based on individual behaviour or traits is high-risk under Annex III point 4(b).

assumptions: Boundary: from the job queue to the closed job; the repair is outside.
Input contract: jobs from the dispatcher in the field service app; fallback is phone and radio.

Technical advice calls keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 for reading the job and calling about unclear ones; s3 keeps 60 and s4 keeps 50 because the technician still reports status and completion, and only waiting for the base and repeating details by radio and phone goes.
Dispatchers' time is outside the technician's savings.
unknowns: Calls to the base per day.
research_questions: Do calls to the base fall?

incremental.description: Telecom technician updates status after leaving areas without coverage.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: poor coverage in rural areas, so much still goes by phone and radio (14.0); high: jobs and status mostly through the app (29.0).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The telecom technician keeps site judgement, diagnosis and technical calls; manual searches, typed notes and status calls shrink.
role.ambitious_version: A technician who spends saved time fixing repeat faults at their source.

job.title: Telecommunications Equipment Installers and Repairers, Except Line Installers
